title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building a purely set-theoretic, point-free-of-topology model of a 1-dimensional 'forme' (a tame 1-dimensional space such as a graph or 1-dimensional polyhedron). On p.3 the data are a set L of 'lieux' (places), a set S of 'segments', a map I ↦ Ĩ ⊂ L (places on I) and a map ∂: S → P_2(L) (two endpoints) with ∂I ⊂ Ĩ. A place is regular if it is interior to some segment and singular otherwise (critical or branch places). This page does two things.

(1) Specialization. y is a specialization of x if y is singular and there is a segment I with x ∈ Ĩ° = Ĩ \ ∂I and y ∈ ∂I. This is the specialization order of the finite T0 (Alexandrov) space attached to a graph: open 'edge' points specialize to closed 'vertex' points. Here, though, the generic objects are the regular places themselves rather than whole edges. It anticipates passing from the point-set model to a stratified or combinatorial (poset) description.

(2) Axioms, drafted and mostly struck through, then rewritten cleanly on p.5.
- F1, decomposability ('décomposabilité des segments'): Ĩ° is nonempty. For z ∈ Ĩ° with ∂I = {x,y} there are unique sub-segments I_{x,z} and I_{y,z} inside Ĩ with the expected endpoints and Ĩ_{x,z} ∩ Ĩ_{y,z} = {z}.
- Added afterwards: (i) a margin warning that one must also require Ĩ = Ĩ_{x,z} ∪ Ĩ_{y,z}; (ii) any sub-segment J ⊂ Ĩ having z as an endpoint lies in Ĩ_{x,z} or in Ĩ_{y,z}.
- First F2 (struck): for a finite set Φ of places in Ĩ° there is a segment I' with Φ ⊂ Ĩ'° and Ĩ' ⊂ Ĩ°. Its corollaries: Ĩ is infinite, and S is infinite if nonempty.
- Second F2, 'réciproque de F1', gluing ('recollement des segments'): if ∂I' ∩ ∂I'' = {z} with z regular, there is a unique I with Ĩ = Ĩ' ∪ Ĩ'' and ∂I = (∂I' ∪ ∂I'') \ {z}.
- A 'Filtration' fragment: two segments whose interiors both contain x contain a common segment around x in the intersection of their interiors. This is a local-basis or filtered-system condition, i.e. the germ of a topology.
- F3 (struck): a finite subset of Ĩ° is contained in some segment lying inside Ĩ°.

The aim is an intrinsic axiomatics of 1-dimensional tame shapes in terms of arcs, endpoints, subdivision and concatenation, presumably as a first step of the 'géométrie des formes' programme.
errors: Gluing axiom as written is false. Grothendieck crossed out the hypothesis Ĩ' ∩ Ĩ'' = and kept only ∂I' ∩ ∂I'' = {z} with z regular. Counterexample in the real line: I' = [0,1] and I'' = [1/2,1], or I' = [0,1] and I'' = [1,2] where I'' overlaps on the other side of a circle. Here the endpoint sets meet in one regular point, yet the union is not a segment with the stated boundary. The hypothesis Ĩ' ∩ Ĩ'' = {z} is needed.
The first version of F1 lacks the covering condition Ĩ = Ĩ_{x,z} ∪ Ĩ_{y,z}. Grothendieck flags this himself ('il faut que ... !!!'). Without it, Ĩ could contain places off both halves.
The corollary 'Ĩ is infinite' follows from iterating F1 (nonempty interiors plus Ĩ_{x,z} ∩ Ĩ_{y,z} = {z}). It does not need the struck F2 'finite Φ' axiom; p.5 indeed attributes it to divisibility.
In the struck F2, 'Φ ∈ Ĩ°' should read Φ ⊂ Ĩ°.

ideas.what: Specialization relation from regular places (interior of a segment) to singular endpoints
ideas.modern_name: Specialization order of the face poset / finite T0 model of a graph; stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937), McCord (1966) for finite models; stratified spaces folklore
ideas.where_published: Spirit of the 'dévissage' of tame stratified spaces in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6, not this definition

ideas.what: Axiomatics of arcs: subdivision of a segment at an interior point with uniqueness of sub-segments
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pasch, Hilbert (order axioms); Ward, Bowditch (pretrees) for 1-dim continua/trees

ideas.what: Gluing (concatenation) of two segments at a regular common endpoint
Filtration condition: segments around a point form a downward directed system
ideas.modern_name: Neighbourhood basis / directed system defining a topology

missed.claim: A topology-free axiomatics of 1-dimensional tame 'forms' via places, segments, decomposition and gluing. It is meant as the base case of a 'géométrie des formes' related to the tame topology of Esquisse d'un programme. It is unfinished and draft-level here.
missed.quote: décomposabilité des segments ... recollement des segments
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly relevant to synthetic or combinatorial models of tame (o-minimal) 1-dimensional sets. However, analogous arc and betweenness axiomatics already exist (pretrees, interval spaces), so novelty is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: Preliminary, partly erroneous draft of standard-flavoured axioms (betweenness, subdivision, concatenation) for 1-dimensional shapes. Of historical interest as part of the 1986 'formes' project, but there is no result unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Struck F2: 'Φ ∈ Ĩ°' should be 'Φ ⊂ Ĩ°' (Φ a finite set of places).
F1: '∃! I_{x,z} ∈ S, I_{y,z} ∈ S' — uniqueness is asserted.
Top-right addition reads approximately: 'Ajouter: ∀J ∈ S tel que J̃ ⊂ Ĩ, ∂J ∋ z, on a J̃ ⊂ Ĩ_{x,z} ou ...'.
Gluing axiom conclusion appears as 'Ĩ' ∪ Ĩ'' ⊂ Ĩ' in the image (later = intended); Grothendieck replaced 'Ĩ' ∩ Ĩ'' =' by '∂I' ∩ ∂I'' = {z}'.
